title: OOM spiral: tenant isolation + KV quarantine to stop production allocator collapse
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Multiple high-severity customer escalations over the last 36 hours show a recurring pattern: aggressive KV cache compaction + eviction races are producing stale handles and micro-fragmentation in the runtime arena which eventually causes allocator backpressure and GPU OOM cascades. Affected environments: Hosted (burst windows), Dedicated (high-throughput tenants), Private (replicated under heavy tail workloads).

Observed behavior: tenants hit sustained OOMs during long-running batched generation workloads. Host-level metrics show growing 'resident fragments' and a rise in failed slab allocations before the first GPU OOM. KV compaction logs include repeated compactor restarts and tombstone churn. After a compaction cycle, some sessions report 'stale-kv-handle' errors and NIC-level retries increase — correlating with sustained allocator slowdown and eventual OOM.

Why urgent: Multiple enterprise customers with Dedicated reservations and a hosted SLO customer escalated; automatic failover to lower-tier model variants did not prevent user-facing timeouts. We need a short-term stopgap to protect customers and a medium-term fix to heal the KV index and allocator behavior.
impact_summary: 3 customers escalated (1 Dedicated, 1 Hosted PLG, 1 Private on-prem). Intermittent but reproducible under synthetic pre-sequence workloads. Latency SLOs violated and some sessions terminated with OOM. Estimated customer downtime windows: 5-30 minutes per incident prior to mitigation.
reproduction_steps: Run long-batched generation workload (seq_len 2048) with steady concurrent sessions (50-200) against a node with active KV compaction enabled
Trigger prefix cache churn: interleave many short-lived sessions that write/evict keys and cause tombstones to accumulate
Observe allocator metrics: rising slab_free_waiters, slab_fragmentation_ratio > 0.35, and repeated compactor retries in runtime logs
Confirm GPU OOMs within 10-40 minutes in stressed Dedicated pools; Hosted bursts show similar pattern when autoscaling delayed
root_cause_hypothesis: The compactor can race with eviction and background KV indexing, leaving ephemeral handles pointing to relocated entries. These stale handles prevent slabs from being reclaimed cleanly, producing fragmentation that eventually starves the GPU allocator. Compactor restarts exacerbate the situation by reintroducing tombstone churn and leaving the index partially inconsistent across shards. Additionally, the allocator's eviction policy does not mark pages referenced by stale handles as reclaimable, creating a leak-like effect under sustained churn.
immediate_mitigations: Deploy a per-tenant KV quarantine mode: new compaction cycles for flagged tenants are slowed and moved to low-priority background workers
Throttle compactor concurrency (default 4 -> 1) to reduce relocation races
Enable emergency allocator backoff that forces reclaim of unreferenced pages after X retries (configurable), lowering the chance of OOM spike
On Dedicated: pin hot tenants to separate GPU pools and reduce tenant co-tenancy until patch is deployed
Notify Private customers with guidance and an upgrade bundle (see links)
long_term_fixes: Rewrite compactor to perform two-phase handoff with explicit handle versioning and tombstone epoch checks
Add KV index checksums and a resync mechanism to detect and repair partial compaction artifacts on startup
Enhance allocator to track weak handles and provide a 'quarantine reclaim' path that can free pages referenced only by stale handles after safe epoch expiry
Add end-to-end stress + fuzz tests in CI that emulate eviction+compaction races and validate no memory leak over 24h
Improve observability: per-tenant fragment heatmap, compaction-latency and tombstone-churn alerts
rollback_plan: If the hotfix causes regressions, revert compactor concurrency change and allocator backoff separately. Canaryed on non-prod, then Dedicated-low, then Hosted. Rollback path: redeploy runtime-2.4.0 and reset tenant quarantine flags. Communicate rollback to affected customers with incident timeline.
canary_and_rollout_plan: Build patch branch runtime-2.4.1-hotfix with compactor throttle + allocator backoff + quarantine flag
Smoke test on staging with synthetic churn scripts for 6 hours
Canary: deploy to 2 non-critical Dedicated clusters (low traffic) for 4 hours
Stage: deploy to 25% of Hosted traffic (rate-limited) and to Private customers who opt-in via support ticket
Full rollout if no regressions observed for 24 hours with continued monitoring
testing_plan: Create churn harness that creates 1000 short-lived sessions with randomized prefix writes and evictions for 24h
Add guard rails to CI that run the harness nightly and fail on fragmentation ratio > 0.25 or any 'stale-kv-handle' errors
Run fuzz tests that corrupt index pointers to verify resync/repair code paths
Validate on GPUs across all supported driver versions (CUDA 12.x and 11.x variants)
Performance regression test to ensure patch does not increase median token latency by > 5% under baseline workloads
monitoring_and_alerts: Create alert: slab_fragmentation_ratio > 0.3 for 10m per node
Dashboard: per-tenant fragment heatmap and compaction cycle duration
Integrate an automated remediation playbook that triggers tenant quarantine flagging and auto-throttle when thresholds crossed
communication_and_customer_notes: Initial support message sent 2026-03-11: investigating GPU OOMs correlated with KV compaction churn
Customer temporary mitigation: enabling tenant-level quarantine and scheduling maintenance windows (link to support ticket)
Planned patch: runtime-2.4.1-hotfix (ETA 2026-03-15), will coordinate Dedicated maintenance windows
Postmortem to be published in Confluence and linked in customer update after full rollout
owners_and_actions: Ravi Patel: implement allocator backoff and quarantine flag (owner)
Marisol Vega: compactor two-phase design and PR review
Ethan Brooks: QA harness and nightly regression integration
Priya Menon: customer communication and support coordination
Oncall: monitor canary channel and trigger rollback if new OOM patterns emerge
updates: 2026-03-10: Incident triaged after first Dedicated customer alert at 03:22 UTC; created ticket and assigned to Ravi.
2026-03-11: Short-term throttles applied to compactor on affected Dedicated clusters; observed reduction in immediate OOM recurrences.
2026-03-12: Hosted SRE enabled tenant quarantine for top 5 noisy tenants; Hosted OOM incidents dropped by 70% during burst windows.
2026-03-13: Patch branch prepared with allocator backoff; unit tests added for handle-versioning checks.
2026-03-14: Non-prod soak completed (48h) with no OOMs under synthetic churn; initiated Dedicated canary deploy.
2026-03-15: Canary in Dedicated showing stabilized fragment metrics; preparing Hosted 25% rollout and Private customer upgrade emails. Continued monitoring for 24h.
postmortem_tasks: Finalize compactor rewrite RFC and schedule implementation in Q2
Add checksum/resync into node startup path and run repair on impacted clusters
Document playbook and add runbook steps to Console for per-tenant quarantine
Schedule follow-up retrospective with SRE, runtime, and support teams
